prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

MIAMI, Florida (CNN) -- Four men have been arrested in connection with the shooting death of NFL player Sean Taylor, authorities announced Friday evening. Police have more than one confession in the case and the individuals will be charged with murder, said Robert Parker, director of the Miami-Dade Police Department. The suspects were identified as Venjah K. Hunte, 20; Eric Rivera Jr., 17; Jason Scott Mitchell, 17; and Charles Kendrick Lee Wardlow, 18. Additional arrests are possible, Parker said. "The key to solving this case was citizen's tips," he said. Taylor, 24, died Tuesday, a day after he was shot during an apparent burglary at his Miami home. The police investigation revealed the suspects thought the house was empty, Parker said. "They were certainly not looking to go there and kill anyone," he said. "They were expecting a residence that was not occupied, so murder or shooting someone was not their initial motive. ... Their obvious motive was to go there and steal the contents of the house." The men knew Taylor lived at the house, Parker said. At 1:45 a.m. Monday, Taylor's girlfriend, Jackie Garcia, called 911 and said someone had been shot. Authorities have said she told police she was hiding under the bedding during the attack. Garcia did not see what happened and could not provide a suspect description, Parker told reporters on Wednesday. Police said Garcia and Taylor were awakened by noise in the living room, and that Taylor got up and locked the bedroom door, but the door was kicked in and two shots were fired, one striking him in the leg. Garcia tried to call 911 but was unable to, and used her cell phone instead, police said. There was no evidence the line had been cut, Parker said Wednesday. A break-in was also reported eight days earlier, Miami-Dade police said. A police report said someone forced a window open and left a kitchen knife on a bed. Several drawers and a bedroom safe were searched during the break-in, according to the report. Taylor was home unexpectedly because of an injury, his former attorney, Richard Sharpstein, told reporters Tuesday. "I think he was surprised or they were surprised to find him there," he said. Taylor spent four years with the Washington Redskins, but had been out with a sprained right knee. He did not play in Sunday's game against Tampa Bay. Taylor was a first-round pick in the 2004 draft, according to his team's web site. He played at the University of Miami, where he was an All-American in 2003, and was also a high school standout in the city. Dubbing him "the prototype NFL free safety," the Redskins credited Taylor's team-leading tackling prowess for sending him to his first Pro Bowl after 2006. He was regarded as one of the hardest hitting players in the league. Taylor recorded 257 tackles (206 solo) during his brief career, two sacks and seven interceptions. E-mail to a friend . CNN's Rich Phillips contributed to this report. Copyright 2007 CNN. All rights reserved.This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. Associated Press contributed to this report.

MIAMI, Florida (CNN) — Authorities said Friday night that four people had been taken into custody over the fatal shooting of NFL player Sean Taylor.

Miami-Dade Police Department Director Robert Parker said investigators had obtained confessions from more than one suspect and that all four would face murder charges. Police named them as Venjah K. Hunte, 20; Eric Rivera Jr., 17; Jason Scott Mitchell, 17; and Charles Kendrick Lee Wardlow, 18. Parker added that further arrests could follow and credited information from members of the public with helping investigators crack the case.

Taylor, 24, died Tuesday after being shot the previous day during what appeared to be a burglary at his Miami residence.

According to Parker, investigators determined that the suspects went to the property believing no one would be home. Their original intention was not to shoot or kill anyone, he said, but to enter the unoccupied house and steal its contents. The men were aware that Taylor lived there.

At approximately 1:45 a.m. Monday, Taylor’s girlfriend, Jackie Garcia, contacted 911 to report that someone had been shot. Authorities said she told them she had hidden beneath the bedding while the attack took place. Parker said Wednesday that Garcia did not witness the shooting and therefore could not describe the intruders.

Police said noise from the living room awakened Garcia and Taylor. Taylor rose and locked the bedroom door, but someone kicked it open and fired twice. One bullet struck Taylor in the leg. Garcia initially tried unsuccessfully to reach 911 through another phone before using her mobile phone. Parker said Wednesday that investigators found no indication that the telephone line had been severed.

Miami-Dade police also disclosed that another break-in had occurred at the home eight days earlier. According to a police report, an intruder forced open a window and left a kitchen knife on a bed. The person also went through multiple drawers and examined a safe in a bedroom.

Richard Sharpstein, Taylor’s former attorney, told reporters Tuesday that an injury had caused Taylor to be at home when he normally would not have been. Sharpstein said either Taylor, the intruders, or both sides apparently were surprised by the encounter.

Taylor played for the Washington Redskins for four seasons but had recently been sidelined by a sprain in his right knee. He missed the team’s Sunday game against Tampa Bay.

The Redskins’ website said Taylor was selected in the first round of the 2004 NFL draft. Before entering the league, he played for the University of Miami, earning All-American recognition in 2003, and had also been a prominent high school athlete in Miami.

The team described Taylor as the model of an NFL free safety and said his team-best tackling performance helped earn him his first Pro Bowl selection following the 2006 season. He was widely considered among the league’s most forceful hitters.

Over his short professional career, Taylor accumulated 257 tackles, including 206 solo stops, along with two sacks and seven interceptions.

CNN’s Rich Phillips contributed to the report, as did The Associated Press. Copyright 2007 CNN. All rights reserved. The material may not be published, aired, rewritten, or redistributed.

Miami-Dade police arrested four men in connection with the fatal shooting of Washington Redskins safety Sean Taylor, saying the suspects traveled from the Fort Myers area to burglarize his home.

The arrests followed an investigation into what authorities described as an apparent burglary that turned deadly. Police said crucial tips from members of the public helped detectives identify the suspects, and investigators obtained confessions from more than one of the men.

Taylor, 24, was shot in the upper leg after confronting intruders inside his Palmetto Bay home. The bullet damaged his femoral artery, causing severe blood loss, and he died at a hospital the following day. His girlfriend and young daughter, who were also in the house, were not injured.

Investigators concluded that the group believed Taylor would be away and that the residence would be empty. Their apparent objective was robbery, police said, rather than a planned killing. Taylor had been home because an injury kept him from traveling with his team.

Authorities nevertheless said the suspects would face murder charges because the death occurred during the commission of a felony. Additional charges related to the break-in and attempted robbery were also expected. Police emphasized that the investigation remained active and said further arrests were possible.
